newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON HEADS U.S. WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS TEAM.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON HEADS U.S. WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS TEAM.

text.p: Olympic double gold medalist Michael Johnson and six other defending world champions will represent the United States in next month's world championships, USA Track & Field announced on Wednesday.

Johnson, winner of the Atlanta Olympics men's 200 and 400 meters, will compete in the men's 400 meters at the August 1-10 world championships in Athens. He also will be a member of the U.S. men's 4x400-meter relay pool.

The 1995 world champion at 200 and 400 meters was given a wild-card entry into the championships by the IAAF, the world governing body for the sport, after he missed the U.S. trials because of injury.

World champions Gail Devers and Gwen Torrence also will compete thanks to wild cards. Devers, the two-time women's 100-meter hurdles gold medalist, will anchor the U.S. women's 4x100-meter relay team and Torrence will defend her women's 100-meter title.
World men's shot put champion John Godina also received a wild-card invitation. He already was a member of the U.S. team in the discus and will compete in both events at Athens.

The strong American team also features new sprint stars Maurice Greene and Marion Jones as well as 110-meter hurdler Allen Johnson, 400-meter hurdler Derrick Adkins and women's 400-meter hurdler Kin Batten. The latter three won gold medals at the 1995 world championships in Gothenburg, Sweden.
Randy Barnes, the Olympic shot put champion, and Kenny Harrison, the men's triple jump gold medalist in Atlanta, also are team members.
